# Retained domain SVG witnesses

All SVGs in this directory are unchanged public outputs from the 2026-10-31
campaign or its publication evidence. `provenance.json` records their exact
source case, producer/version where recorded, original retained path, source
SHA-256 and decompressed SVG SHA-256. No renderer runs in these tests. Tests
resolve expectations through the already independently reviewed literal source
corpus or the authored source contracts, never through these outputs.

The domain observer uses browser paint and geometry, table rows, physical
connector endpoints, actual marker shapes, calendar/score ticks, rooted tree
stems, ordered columns, boolean circle intersections and railroad wiring. Its
function is serialized into the browser; SVG IDs/classes and native models do
not select semantics. Functional SVG references such as marker/filter URLs are
resolved only to inspect their actual physical contents.

Important closed-profile encodings come from the public source pin
`1fb7869866dd619168d840291c9c54b4f129758b`:

- `diagrams/user-journey/svgDraw.js:211–219` ends the task stem at score zero
  and uses one visible face diameter per score unit. This independently fixes
  an absolute scale without fitting against expected scores. A second public
  vocabulary supplies printed numeric score ticks instead.
- `diagrams/eventmodeling/db.ts:290–324` defines the default type palette;
  `:580–617` describes reset/explicit-read/previous-different-lane effects.
  Other palettes without source-owned color requests remain unknown.
  `:189–203,336` splits exactly two qualified identity segments into the
  actual caption and its typed namespace lane; both owned parts are required.
- `diagrams/treeView/renderer.ts:146` combines rowIndent with the default
  five-unit horizontal padding. Measured hierarchy stems independently prove
  the rows; requested font/color/line properties bind actual paint.
- `diagrams/pie/pieRenderer.ts:53–65` defines the donut/text-position ratios;
  the pie stylesheet defines the explicit 1.05 scale and opacity distinction
  of a highlighted slice. Geometry must establish those effects independently.
- `docs/syntax/gitgraph.md:505–568` defines visible branch-lane precedence.
  Empty branches preserve their names and order without inventing a printed
  native head pointer; committed branches retain measured head obligations.
- Independently transcribed theme constants and CSS HSL formulas are in
  `fidelity/theme-source-policy.ts` and `docs/evidence/source-theme-policy.json`.
  Exact owned foreground/background/alpha roles remain required. Zero-alpha
  curve fill compares the composed visible effect; hidden RGB supplies no credit.

Wardley `evolve` targets are checked at the **painted arrow tip**, with two CSS
pixels of measurement tolerance. The retained Mermaid basic example has tips
about 7.4 pixels short of its declared targets and is a retained real negative.
Its source implementation subtracts a node radius plus two units from the
stem, but no future target circle is visible and the documentation grants no
such target allowance. A physical repair control places the visible tips at
the literal declared coordinates. This defect is not excused by reference
renderer agreement or a tolerance fitted to its output.

Wardley pipeline parents use the source-reviewed `pipeline-group` projection:
the actual labelled range and every member glyph share the required visibility,
and every member preserves its exact evolution. The original standalone parent
coordinate remains in the full native/advisory source profile.

Unprinted Git operation history, grammar syntax dialect and radial mindmap
source traversal remain exact native/advisory metadata under independent source
review; no drawing observer pretends to recover those identities. Required
visual obligations remain unknown for external icon identity,
unqualified mixed/outlined labels, unsupported calendar/status skins,
annotations/configuration without a complete projection, and uninspectable
wiring. Such cases receive no complete drawing credit. The module does not reduce
or rewrite the source contracts.
